correctness.rationale: For fixed image subspaces U and V with overlap u, all four relations are equivalent to two independent quotient surjections E/(U+V) onto U and V. Gaussian counting gives the exact number of pairs (U,V), and independent full-row-rank matrix counts give both surjection factors. All degenerate cases and nonvanishing conditions are explicit, including r=0, s=0, u=0 and d=0. Exhaustive direct matrix calculations over q=2,3,4 for n up to 4 (as listed in VERIFICATION.md) match every stratum. The finite checks are supplementary rather than a substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: The same objects appear in Morrison (1980, §5) and Schröer (arXiv:math/0211293; 2004); their results classify orbits, components and degenerations, not the finite-field three-parameter point counts. Bleher–Chinburg–Huisgen-Zimmermann (arXiv:1407.3045) likewise studies component and generic geometry. Oblak (arXiv:math/0612300) studies possible Jordan types, and Huang (arXiv:2110.15566, §3.1) counts unrestricted annihilating matrices without simultaneous square-zero and rank/image-overlap refinement. The explicit joint count is not supplied by the examined statements and is not a consequence of component cardinality or Jordan admissibility alone. The factorization into quotient maps is classical and credited; an equivalent Hall-polynomial formulation may exist outside inspected sources.
residual_risks: Equivalent formulas may be implicit in Hall-polynomial methods for Kronecker representations or outside indexed works.
The quotient-map idea predates this counting result; new content is the complete explicitly weighted triple distribution, not module-theoretic normal forms.
The source comparison is not independent bibliographic certification.

value.rationale: The invariant counts all labeled modules over the natural two-loop radical-square-zero algebra, refining its radical layering and the two individual Jordan ranks by their image intersection. It is a complete nonempty-stratum and cardinality classification for every n and finite field, not a selected small case. Exact point counts complement classical geometric component descriptions and make the extreme overlap rigidity quantitative. Because the joint invariant is determined explicitly across a natural full representation family, it has independent enumerative value even without a new orbit theorem.
